description: The shared contract between normalizeFontKey() in src/detail/font_key.h and
normalize_font_key() in tools/font_keys.py. Two implementations are
unavoidable - the C++ normalizes caller input at runtime, the Python
normalizes at generation time to emit the table keys - so they are pinned
here instead. tests/font_key_test.py checks the Python against these vectors
and confirms tests/font_key_vectors.h is current; tests/font_key_tests.cpp
checks the C++ against the same rows via that generated header.
Add a vector whenever the rule changes. A case that only one language can
get right is the bug this file exists to catch.

vectors.note: the ordinary case: fold case, drop the space
leading, interior and trailing runs all collapse away
tab, newline and carriage return are ASCII whitespace
vertical tab and form feed complete the six ASCII whitespace chars
whitespace-only normalizes to the empty key, which matches nothing
the comma survives; without it this would become 'maestrotimes', a real font, silently answering a MusicXML font-family list with the wrong face
punctuation is not folded, so a PostScript name does not masquerade as its family
U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE is NOT removed; Python's str.split() would have, the C++ never would, and the generator must not mint a key the runtime cannot reach
U+0085 NEXT LINE: whitespace to Python's str.split(), not to this rule
U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE: likewise left alone
U+001C FILE SEPARATOR is plain ASCII and still not whitespace here, though str.split() drops it
a real legacy font, so the C++ side can also confirm this key resolves
a real legacy font reached by an all-caps spelling
a real SMuFL registry font, exercising the same key on the registry side

the leading A-umlaut stays UPPERCASE: only A-Z are folded. Python's str.lower() would have lowercased it, and std::tolower() under a Latin-1 locale would have rewritten bytes inside the UTF-8 sequence - either one would put a key in the table that the other language could never produce
multi-byte UTF-8 survives intact, whether walked as characters or as bytes
